title: The overdue book
summary: A library sends a letter about a book that was borrowed forty years ago.
paragraphs: One morning, a letter arrived at the García house. It was from the town library, and it was for Mr Andrés García, who was seventy-one. "Dear reader," it said, "our records show that you borrowed the book Sailing for Beginners on 3 March 1985. It is now {{overdue}}. Please return it as soon as possible."

Mr García laughed so much that he had to sit down. Then he went quiet. He remembered the book. He had borrowed it when he was thirty, because he dreamed of buying a small boat and sailing along the coast. Then his first daughter was born, he got a new job, and the dream, and the book, went into a box in the {{attic}}.

His granddaughter Sofía helped him look for it. They opened boxes of old photos, school reports and letters. At the bottom of the fifth box, under a broken radio, they found it. The cover was faded, and there were notes in pencil in the {{margins}}: "Try this!", "Ask Paco about knots", "Summer?"

They took the book back to the library together. The librarian, a young man with green glasses, explained that the library was moving to a new computer system, and the old records had produced hundreds of strange letters. "Don't worry," he said. "There's no {{fine}}." Then he looked at the notes in the margins. "Did you ever go sailing?" he asked. Mr García shook his head.

The librarian smiled and wrote something on a piece of paper. It was the name of a sailing club at the port that gave lessons to adults of any age. Last month, Mr García had his first lesson. He was slow and nervous, and he fell into the water once. But at the end of the lesson, he {{steered}} the boat back into the port by himself. Sofía took a photo, and he put it inside the cover of a new copy of the book, which he bought and did not have to return.

overdue.meaning: not returned or done by the time it should be

attic.meaning: the room or space under the roof of a house

margins.meaning: the empty spaces at the sides of a page

fine.meaning: money you have to pay because you broke a rule

steered.meaning: controlled the direction of a boat or car

questions.question: Why did the library write to Mr García?
options: He had lost his library card.
Their records showed a book he borrowed in 1985.
They wanted him to give a talk.
questions.explanation: The letter said he borrowed Sailing for Beginners in 1985 and it was overdue.

questions.question: Why did he never use the book?
options: His daughter was born and he got a new job.
The book was in another language.
questions.explanation: His first daughter was born, he got a new job, and the dream went into a box.

questions.question: Why did the library send so many strange letters?
options: The library was moving to a new computer system.
The librarian made a mistake on purpose.
questions.explanation: The old records had produced hundreds of strange letters during the move to a new system.

questions.question: What did the librarian give Mr García?
options: The name of a sailing club with lessons for adults
A new copy of the book
questions.explanation: He wrote down the name of a sailing club that gave lessons to adults.
